**Remove obsolete derived content when an event is replaced.**

If a previously indexable event is replaced with empty text, this loop queues no replacement derived event. The earlier `graph.node:derive:*` event and its embedding remain, although Line 598 removes its owned edges. The same problem applies when changed graph-node text produces different chunk or sentence IDs. Record ownership for derived events and embeddings, then remove obsolete owned rows during replacement. Otherwise, old content can remain stored indefinitely when event TTL is disabled. **Refresh embedding ownership when the source changes.**

If two `graph.node` events use the same `node_id` and raw text, this comparison skips the second event even when its `source_event_id` or `project` differs. The stored embedding keeps the first event's ownership and project. The scoped recall reader filters embedding rows by those fields, so a newly admitted source can remain without a usable index. Compare the binding fields as well, and update metadata when the vector itself does not need regeneration.
